story: Prometheus, a Titan, was responsible for creating humanity from clay and aiding it in its earliest days. He was regarded as the father of human arts and sciences, and in some accounts the father of Deucalion, the hero of a flood story. At a sacrificial meal meant to settle accounts between mortals and immortals, Prometheus tricked Zeus, king of the Olympian gods, by offering him a choice between beef hidden inside an ox's stomach and bones wrapped in glistening fat. Zeus chose the fat-wrapped bones, and this became the precedent for future sacrifices, with humans keeping the meat and burning bones for the gods. Angered by the trick, Zeus hid fire from humanity. Prometheus stole the fire back, hidden in a fennel stalk, and restored it to humanity. In retaliation, Zeus had Hephaestus fashion the first woman out of clay, with Athena helping to adorn her. She carried a jar which, when opened, released mischief, sorrow, plague, and disease into the world; only Hope remained trapped inside because the jar was sealed before it could escape. For his crimes, Zeus bound Prometheus to a rock in the Caucasus Mountains and sent an eagle to eat his liver daily; the liver regrew each night, prolonging the torment. Eventually, the hero Heracles killed the eagle and freed Prometheus, with Zeus's permission. In another tradition, Prometheus was also credited with establishing the form of animal sacrifice practiced in religious ritual.
